earlier_scan.source_named: Only sociolinguistic surveys/wordlists (Webster 1992, 2022) and van Driem 2001 overview in Glottolog; no phonological description of Kutang Ghale located.

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing & Dolma Choekyi Lama. 2025-2026. Documenting Kuke: the linguistic ecology of a 'stolen' language in Nepal. ELAR collection dk0839 (ELDP small grant, University of Sydney; hdl:2196/3bd9079a-36c8-4c70-92e0-80b7efe66b55).
sources.note: Collection landing page and ELDP project blurb read: audio-video corpus (conversations, elicitation, ELAN/Toolbox files); 'Language information' text covers speaker numbers, contact history and the 'stolen language' etymology only; nothing on phonology, tone or stress; no grammar/sketch listed yet.

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing. 2023. Segmental and prosodic phonology and morphophonology in Tsum, a language of Nepal. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl:1885/307369).
sources.note: Describes TSUM (Tibetic neighbour), not Kuke. Kutang Ghale appears only in Table 1.2 (neighbouring Tamangic language) and p.13 (27% lexical similarity with Tsum per Webster 2022:10). No statement about Kuke phonology or stress. Saved because the author now holds the ELDP Kuke documentation grant.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages, Part 2, ch.10.7.3 (Tamangic contact languages).
sources.note: Only lists 'Kutang Ghale' among Tamangic languages (after Mazaudon 1978); nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-169: Ghale, Kutang [ght] -> additional name Kuke (submitted by Melissa Ryan & Mari-Sisko Khadgi). SIL International. 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Identity/name background only; p.2 states 'To our knowledge there has been no linguistic research done among the Kuke language people after 1992, except Mari-Sisko Khagdi's small-scale survey in 2006'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kutang language' (citing Ethnologue 18 and Childs 2004 Tibetan Diary).
sources.note: No phonology section; dialects Bihi, Chak, Rana; sources are Ethnologue and Childs 2004 (ethnography).

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing (University of Sydney). In progress, 2025-. Outputs of ELDP project 'Documenting Kuke: the linguistic ecology of a stolen language in Nepal' (ELAR dk0839): expected phonological sketch / conference papers on Kuke.

sources.note: First trained-phonologist documentation of Kuke (the depositor wrote a prosodic-phonology PhD on neighbouring Tsum); a sketch or talk handout would be the first description of Kuke tone/stress. Worth contacting the depositor or re-checking ELAR/ALS/HLS abstracts in 2026-27.
